observation_summary: The class VerificationOverTimeImpl was causing LinkageErrors (VerifyError/NoClassDefFoundError) because it explicitly referenced a JUnit-dependent exception class (ArgumentsAreDifferent) in a catch block, even when JUnit was not present on the classpath.
reasoning_summary: The fix involved changing the exception type in a catch block from a specific class that had an unwanted dependency (ArgumentsAreDifferent) to a more generic, built-in type (AssertionError). This is a correction of the procedural logic (the exception handling strategy) to avoid an unnecessary dependency, which fits the Algorithm/Method category as it modifies the local computational/control flow strategy.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows changing 'catch (org.mockito.exceptions.verification.junit.ArgumentsAreDifferent e)' to 'catch (AssertionError e)'.

The bug report states that the class 'VerificationOverTimeImpl' uses a try/catch block with an exception that extends 'junit.framework.ComparisonFailure', causing runtime linking errors when JUnit is missing.
The stack trace confirms LinkageErrors (VerifyError/NoClassDefFoundError) occurring at runtime due to the class loader failing to resolve the JUnit-dependent class.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the issue involves a dependency on an external class, the fix is not changing an API signature or a contract between components, but rather changing the internal exception handling logic within a single method.
The fix is not adding a missing guard or validation check, but rather changing the type of exception being caught in an existing catch block.
